newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BEATS KORDA IN TENSE HALLE FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BEATS KORDA IN TENSE HALLE FINAL.

text.p: Top seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov saved three match points to beat Petr Korda of the Czech Republic 7-6 6-7 7-6 in the final of the Halle grasscourt tournament on Sunday.
In winning the first grasscourt tournament of his career, the 23-year-old Russian avenged a defeat in last year's final to Nicklas Kulti of Sweden, while for Korda it was a 15th final loss.
Kafelnikov, ranked six in the world, clinched the title with his first match point after two hours and 18 minutes.
The Russian, who broke his racquet after slamming it into the ground late in the final tiebreaker, said he was fortunate to win the tiebreaker-filled match.

"I was lucky at the end to win," Kafelnikov said of his 12th tournament win. "It has been a long time since I won an ATP tournament. But this year has started well with this first tournament win in Halle."
The 1996 French Open champion, who defeated local hero Boris Becker in a semifinal on Saturday, was out-served by Korda, hitting only seven aces compared to his rival's 28.
Korda had to send for an extra pair of shoes from Prague on Saturday night because he did not expect to reach the final and had not packed enough tennis shoes.
The Russian won the first set tiebreaker 7-2, but Korda rallied to take the second 7-5.
The Czech player looked certain to win the tiebreaker in the third set, but Kafelnikov saved three match points before going ahead for the first time 8-7 and then held serve to win.
